children: A slight improvement in Germany's ifo business climate index in November signals solid economic growth in the final quarter of this year, Andrew Kenningham at Capital Economics says in a note. "We expect this to continue into the new year," he says. The index rose to 90.6 this month, from 90.1 in October, which points to growth of around 0.7% in the fourth quarter, Kenningham says. "We suspect growth will be closer to 0.3% but that would still be a bit better than the third quarter and would bring the annual growth rate this year to 1%." Looking ahead, fiscal stimulus is expected to continue boosting investment, which in addition to a strong outlook for exports should keep momentum going next year, Kenningham says. (don.forbes@wsj.com)
